prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your specific needs (complexity of the case, medical history, bone loss, aesthetic expectations) and on the training and teamwork behind the treatment. That said, you’ll usually get the best outcomes by involving a specialist team: a qualified surgeon to place the implant and an experienced restorative dentist or prosthodontist to restore it.

How to find the best implant provider in Columbus, OH
- Prioritize specialty and training
  - Oral and maxillofacial surgeon (OMS) or periodontist for implant placement. Both have advanced surgical training.
  - Prosthodontist or an implant-experienced restorative dentist for the crown/bridge restoration.
  - Look for additional implant-specific training (fellowships, AAID fellowship, continuing education courses) and certification where applicable.

- Check credentials and experience
  - Years of implant experience and number of implants placed.
  - Experience with full-arch, bone grafting, sinus lifts, immediate-load/All-on-4 if you need those.
  - Use CBCT (3D) imaging and digital planning — important for predictable results.

- Read reviews and see before/after cases
  - Google Reviews, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Yelp — look for consistent positive feedback and photos of actual cases.
  - Ask to see before/after photos of cases similar to yours.

- Ask the right questions at a consult
  - How many implants have you placed? How many cases like mine?
  - Are you a specialist (OMS/periodontist/prosthodontist)? Where did you train?
  - Will you use CBCT and guided surgical planning?
  - What implant system do you use and why?
  - Who will do the crown/restoration? Is that done in-house or by a separate dentist?
  - What are the risks, success rate, and expected timeline and cost?
  - Do you perform bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed?

- Verify reputation and safety
  - Check ADA, AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons), AAP (American Academy of Periodontology), AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) listings.
  - Confirm state dental board status for any disciplinary history.

- Red flags
  - Vague answers about experience or implant system.
  - No CBCT or no treatment plan.
  - Extremely low price compared with local averages (could mean lower-quality implants or no proper planning).

Where to look right now
- ADA Find-a-Dentist, AAOMS and AAP/AAID “find a specialist” tools.
- Local reviews on Google, Healthgrades, Zocdoc.
- Ask your general dentist for a trusted referral (they often refer to surgeons they trust and coordinate care).

If you’d like, I can:
- Help you draft a short list of questions to ask during a consultation.
- Prepare an email or phone script to contact practices.
- Search for top-rated implant specialists in Columbus if you give me a ZIP code (note: I can’t browse the web directly in this chat unless you want guidance on how to search).
